(Index continues directly from the existing endpoint a(7). ALL three terms are certified
dual-lineage: Lineage 1 (Claude) = explicit construction of the halved n-cube graph (vertices =
even-Hamming-weight length-n bitstrings, 2^(n-1) of them; edges between vectors at Hamming
distance 2) + from-scratch fraction-free Gaussian elimination (Bareiss) on the exact integer
Laplacian cofactor. Lineage 2 (Codex, independently authored, no access to Lineage-1 code) =
same explicit construction for the a(8)/a(9) gate check (matching sympy Bareiss for a(9) as a
sanity cross-check), then for a(8)-a(10) an exact modular-cofactor-determinant + CRT
reconstruction exploiting the graph's abelian (Z_2^n) Cayley structure via Walsh/Hadamard
diagonalization, certified by an integer Hadamard bound. Both lineages reproduce every published
term (a(1)..a(7)) exactly and agree digit-for-digit on a(8), a(9), a(10).)

## 2. Ready-to-paste comment / annotation

a(8)-a(10) computed via Kirchhoff's Matrix-Tree theorem on the explicit halved n-cube graph
(vertices = even-weight length-n bitstrings, 2^(n-1) of them, edges at Hamming distance 2): the
Laplacian cofactor was evaluated as an exact big-integer determinant by two independently
implemented methods — fraction-free Gaussian elimination (Bareiss) and a multi-modular-
determinant-plus-CRT reconstruction exploiting the graph's Z_2^n Cayley/Walsh-Hadamard structure,
certified by an explicit Hadamard bound — and they agree digit-for-digit on all three new terms,
both also reproducing every one of the seven previously published terms (a(1)..a(7)) exactly.
Runtime for a(10) (512 vertices, 511x511 cofactor): under 3 minutes for the direct Bareiss
lineage, under a second for the Walsh-diagonalized modular lineage; peak RSS well under 600MB
for either.
